skill.name: Take account of the other side
skill.why: Answering the other side makes an argument much harder to knock down.
skill.how: Look for both halves: what the other side thinks, then the writer's answer.

beats.say: Good arguers don't pretend the other side isn't there.
First, they say what the other side thinks.
beats.show: **Some people say** my custard is too lumpy.

beats.say: Then they answer it with a reason.
Both halves together take account of the other side.
beats.show: **Some say it's lumpy,** **but the lumps are real banana.**

beats.say: Only one half? Then it doesn't count.

encounters.text: SAVE CORAL GULLY, by marine scientist Dr Lena Moss. Coral Gully, on the northern side of Bluster Rock, is home to the island's last healthy patch of reef. In the past five years, our surveys have found that the number of fish on the reef has fallen by almost half, and the giant clams that once lined the gully have nearly disappeared. I believe the council should make Coral Gully a no-fishing sanctuary, where the reef can rest and recover. Some fishing families fear the sanctuary will leave their nets empty, but at Pelican Point, catches just outside a sanctuary doubled within ten years. That happens because fish grow large and breed inside the protected area, then spill out into the surrounding water. Healthy reefs also attract snorkellers, who spend money in local cafes, dive shops and caravan parks. Some people say the council cannot afford new signs and patrol boats. The decision will be made at the council meeting on the first Monday of next month, and I urge every resident who cares about the reef to come along and speak up. Children are welcome too, and the surf club will run a free sausage sizzle afterwards. Copies of our survey results are available at the library.

encounters.text: Speech by Rosa Delgado, street musician. I have played my guitar outside the Bluster Rock bakery every Saturday morning for six years. In that time, I've played for tourists, toddlers, grumpy truck drivers and one very confused emu. I want to talk about the proposal to ban busking in the mall. I understand that some shop owners find the music distracting, and a few have said that it makes it hard to talk to customers. I hear them. But a simple rule that buskers must move every hour and keep the volume low would fix that problem, without silencing anyone. Music brings people into the mall, and people who stop to listen often stay to buy a coffee or a pie. The bakery owner, Mr Lam, told me his Saturday sales are the best of the week. Other towns have tried banning buskers, and some say their main streets became quiet and empty. Please don't make that mistake here. Let the music stay, and let's write some fair rules together. Rosa finished her speech by playing a short song she had written about the mall, and three councillors tapped their feet. One of them even hummed along on the way out of the meeting. The vote will be held next month.

encounters.text:
KEEP THE LANTERN TOURS, by Ezra Finch, tour guide. For twelve years, the Lantern Tours have led visitors through the old Bluster Rock cemetery after dark, telling the true stories of the miners, cooks and camel drivers who built this town. Each tour raises money to repair the crumbling headstones, and last year we fixed thirty-one of them. Visitors come from all over the country, and many are descendants of the people buried there, hoping to learn more about their own families. Without the tours, these stories would be forgotten, and the headstones would keep falling apart.

Some neighbours have complained that the tours are noisy, and that torch beams shine through their bedroom windows late at night. They are right, and I am sorry. From next month, every tour will finish by half past eight, and our guides will use red lanterns, which are far dimmer than torches. We will also stay on the paths at the far end, well away from the houses.

The Lantern Tours bring history to life in a way no textbook can. Last month, a Year 5 class joined a tour and wrote a whole book about the camel drivers. Our guides are all volunteers, and they would be heartbroken to stop. I hope the council will let them continue.
